solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: PC that is right for item of office kit

parts.note: a PC (police constable) is a cop
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A personal computer is the right choice of equipment for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer, which fits the office scene, but here it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier is a standard machine found in workplaces, so it is an item of office equipment.

clue.text: Who's always right finds me so curt, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shopper who is never wrong complains about brusque service.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the retail saying that the customer is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: The shop proverb says the buyer is always right, so the person described is the shopper.

clue.text: In favour of long sentences? Then think highly of spread

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a life sentence is the longest prison term
to rate someone is to esteem them

explanation.surface: A writer likes long sentences and admires wide coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Long sentences suggests wordy prose, but means prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply and spread rapidly, so the verb matches spread.

clue.text: Being overturned, Mike to dismiss test

indicators.note: overturned in a down entry means flipped upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to axe someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: After a ruling is overturned, Mike is told to drop the test.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal assessment of knowledge, so it is a test.

clue.text: European Parliament border on time that's transitory

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: things that are transitory

parts.note: EP is the abbreviation for European Parliament
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something about the European Parliament bordering on short-lived business.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an adjective phrase, but it stands for the plural noun: items that are short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that last only a short while, such as printed matter meant to be thrown away.

clue.text: I go on quiet train?

definitions.note: spoken by the answer: one who talks on and on

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a rattler is old slang for a train

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether to board the quiet coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: a chatterer would say this of themselves, ironic beside a quiet carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prattler chatters at length about trivia, so such a person keeps talking, going on and on.

clue.text: Delightful new song, one in English

indicators.note: in places the earlier items inside the last one

parts.note: Eng is the abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for new
a chant is a simple song
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lovely fresh song, one sung in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanting means charming, casting a spell of pleasure, so it means delightful.

clue.text: The Muses conceal a fast runner

indicators.note: what the words conceal is tucked inside them, read across the gap

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The goddesses of the arts are hiding a sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird that can sprint at high speed.

clue.text: Plant which flowers close to autumn is behind

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of autumn

explanation.surface: A plant that blooms near autumn is late in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Asters are indeed late-flowering, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term meaning at or toward the back of a ship, so behind.

clue.text: Get wind of run in bank

indicators.note: in puts one item inside another

parts.note: to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Hearing of a run on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A run on a bank sounds financial, but bank is the verb to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wind of something is to find out about it, which is to learn of it.

clue.text: Knowing about preposterous rubbish in charge for boxing?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: sage means wise or knowing

indicators.note: preposterous literally means back-to-front (before put after), so the word is turned around

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A know-all comments on absurd nonsense about a boxing match fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing suggests the sport, but it means putting things in boxes; storage is also the fee charged for keeping goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is a fee paid to keep goods in a warehouse, a charge for keeping things boxed up.

clue.text: What makes the room comfortable? Noble narrative

parts.note: AC, air conditioning, keeps a room comfortable
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A noble's tale about what makes a room cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a report or story of events, so it is a synonym for a narrative.

clue.text: Old boring piece for late newspaper article

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a drill bit is the piece that bores holes

explanation.surface: A dull old item filed late for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring reads as dull, but it means drilling; late means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper piece about someone recently deceased, which is the sense of late here.

clue.text: This measures angles for tower

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tractor is something that tows, a tow-er

explanation.surface: A device measuring the angles of a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower looks like a tall building, but read it as tow-er, one that tows: a tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is the semicircular geometry instrument used for measuring degrees of angles.

clue.text: Miserly drunk clasped duke?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
dukes is slang for fists, so a clasped duke is a fist made, fisted

explanation.surface: A stingy, inebriated aristocrat being held.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke looks like a nobleman, but 'put up your dukes' means fists; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight-fisted describes someone who grips money and will not spend it, a miser.

clue.text: Joker with weakness for cups and saucers and the rest

definitions.text: cups and saucers and the rest

parts.note: a teaser is someone who teases, a joker
a vice is a moral weakness

explanation.surface: A prankster with a weakness for crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a matching set of crockery: cups, saucers, teapot, milk jug and so on.

clue.text: Cricket team, say, lodged in hotel eventually

indicators.note: something lodged in the following words sits inside them across the word gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cricket team eventually checks into a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side has eleven players, so the team is itself called an eleven; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Rig vote somehow and you'll get a sickening sensation?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters end up in some new, unspecified arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fixing an election might leave you feeling queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a dizzy, giddy feeling that often brings nausea, so it is a sickening sensation.

clue.text: Salutary member of the clergy accommodating drip of a sort

indicators.note: accommodating means housing a guest, so one item holds the other

parts.note: a curate is an assistant priest
an IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A cleric with a medical drip in place, which proves beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Salutary means beneficial to health, and a curative remedy is one that heals.

clue.text: By which real duty gets sullied?

definitions.text: By which real duty gets sullied?

indicators.note: something sullied is spoiled, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asking what corrupts a true obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: infidelity is the act through which the true marital duty of faithfulness gets tarnished.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is unfaithfulness in marriage, a betrayal of the duty spouses owe each other.

clue.text: Rashly assume Romeo's chap with healing hands

indicators.note: doing something rashly is doing it carelessly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Don't jump to conclusions about Romeo being a healer.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a man who gives massages, working on the body with his hands to relieve aches.

clue.text: Singing from the same hymn sheet in concert

definitions.text: Singing from the same hymn sheet
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for being in full agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves sound musical, but both are idioms for agreement and joint action.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined in purpose, which both idioms describe: shared agreement and acting jointly.

clue.text: Smooch being cut short satisfied fate

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to smooch is to kiss
a demand that is satisfied is met

explanation.surface: A kiss interrupted, yet destiny is fulfilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is Turkish-derived for destiny, the fate that awaits someone.

clue.text: Yard where the sun rises produces fungus

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard
the sun rises in the east

explanation.surface: A sunny back yard grows a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a single-celled fungus used in baking and brewing.

clue.text: One cracking reserve vessel in the arctic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that breaks down shyness or social stiffness
second meaning: a ship that clears a path through frozen sea

explanation.walkthrough: Reserve here is social coolness; breaking the ice means easing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is both a party opener that eases awkwardness and a ship built to smash polar ice.

clue.text: Face set back with feature of old phones

indicators.note: back says the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: laid is a past form of set, as in set or laid down

explanation.surface: A face set into old telephones.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions surround the wordplay: the clock face and the rotary wheel of old telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial is a clock or watch face, and old telephones had a rotary dial for numbers.

clue.text: Chaps capping upper-class list of options

indicators.note: in a down entry a cap sits on top, so one item goes above the other

parts.note: chaps are men
U is the classic label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Fellows topping a list of posh choices.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes, or of computer commands, to choose from.

clue.text: Drink with rifleman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gin and vermouth cocktail
second meaning: Friedrich von ..., designer of the ...-Henry rifle

explanation.walkthrough: The rifleman is not a soldier but the Swiss engineer whose breech-loading action gave the Martini-Henry rifle its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail shares its name with the gunsmith whose action was used in the British army's Victorian rifle.

clue.text: This deserter upset Jack

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: jack and tar are both slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor upset by someone who abandoned ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are said to desert a sinking ship, hence a rat is a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who abandons their side, like rats fleeing a sinking ship.

clue.text: Staff respect changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Employees' regard for the boss shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like employees but is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod a monarch carries, a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Bound by an expression of comfort in little Edward

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
'there, there' is said to comfort someone

explanation.surface: A toddler named Edward soothed and held close.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied by a rope or chain, so the thing is bound and cannot wander.

clue.text: Several hang out on a bright day?

definitions.text: hang out on a bright day?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: to dry in the sunshine, as washing on a line

explanation.walkthrough: Hang out suggests idling, but it means pegging washing out; split the answer as sun-dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or assorted, a near synonym of several, while sun-dry is to dry in sunshine.
